extraction.name: RoboFAC Dataset
extraction.description: A large-scale and diverse dataset for question-answering on robot failure videos, comprising 9,440 erroneous manipulation trajectories and 78,623 QA pairs across 16 diverse tasks and 53 scenes in both simulation and real-world environments. The dataset covers six types of robotic failures across three hierarchical levels (task planning, motion planning, and execution control), with eight question types targeting task understanding, failure analysis, and failure correction.
extraction.creator: Weifeng Lu, Minghao Ye, Zewei Ye, Ruihan Tao, Shuo Yang, Bo Zhao (School of AI, Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Xiamen University; Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen)
extraction.citeAs: Weifeng Lu, Minghao Ye, Zewei Ye, Ruihan Tao, Shuo Yang, Bo Zhao. RoboFAC: A Comprehensive Framework for Robotic Failure Analysis and Correction. arXiv:2505.12224v3 [cs.RO], 25 May 2025.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Simulation data was collected for 14 robotic tasks in the ManiSkill environment, augmented with objects from the YCB Object Dataset and scenes from ReplicaCAD and AI2-THOR. Expert policies were defined by specifying target end-effector poses, and failure data was generated by replacing the expert policy with code snippets that produce erroneous trajectories. Real-world data was collected for 6 tasks via teleoperation using the SO-100 robotic arm. Each video was accompanied by a corresponding textual description.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Software Collection, Experiments
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Simulation data from the ManiSkill environment augmented with objects from the YCB Object Dataset and scenes from ReplicaCAD and AI2-THOR. Real-world data collected via teleoperation using the SO-100 robotic arm. Each video is accompanied by a corresponding textual description including the substage where failure occurred, the taxonomy of failure, and a detailed textual explanation of the error.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Given the motion planning for the robotic arm occasionally failed, resulting in trajectories that did not align with the corresponding textual descriptions, manual data cleaning was performed and approximately 75% of the collected data was retained.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Raw data was annotated to construct video-based QA samples for eight question types. For five question types (task identification, task planning, failure detection, failure identification, and failure locating), reference answers were directly extracted from the textual description. For the remaining three types (failure explanation, high-level correction, and low-level correction), GPT-4o was used with both the video and its corresponding textual description as inputs to generate reference answers. All GPT-4o outputs were manually reviewed and corrected.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: All outputs from GPT-4o used for annotation were manually reviewed and corrected to ensure annotation quality.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The current integration of the RoboFAC model into the VLA-controlled robotic system is not yet seamless. The model is applied exclusively to the VLA model, and the success rate remains subject to further enhancement, largely due to the VLA model's limited ability to follow complex natural language instructions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluation of multimodal large language models for robotic failure analysis and correction, including task understanding, failure detection, failure identification, failure locating, failure explanation, and failure correction (high-level and low-level). The dataset is split into 60K QA pairs for training and 18K QA pairs for evaluation (10K simulated, 8K real-world).

description.evidence: The RoboFAC dataset encompasses robotic tasks of varying complexity, ranging from simple short-horizon tasks to complex long-horizon tasks, and tasks executed in dynamic environments. It includes 14 simulated tasks and 6 real-world tasks, with two of the real-world tasks not present in the simulation environment. The dataset includes six types of failures, spanning three hierarchical levels of error.
